title: Energy-controlled large free subsemigroups inside twofold products for acylindrical actions on hyperbolic length spaces
source_title: Product set growth in Burnside groups
author: Rémi Coulon; Markus Steenbock
difficulty_reason: Acylindricity alone does not select a large strongly reduced alphabet from a finite set with controlled energy. The authors construct an appropriate quasi-center and separately solve the diffuse-energy and concentrated-energy cases by Gromov-product selection and acylindrical packing. Those new extraction arguments produce the precise cardinality and scale bounds before the short final case split.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Independent Theorem8.1: isometric(N,kappa)-acylindrical action on a delta-hyperbolic metric length space, delta>0, kappa>=50000delta, finite U with infinity-energy lambda(U)>100kappa. Exact small-cardinality alternative|U|<=400kappa N/delta or W subset Uv subset U² strongly reduced with alpha<=25kappa and cardinality>=delta|U|/(10^6 N lambda(U)); Lemma3.2 gives free subsemigroup. All new quasi-center stopping proof, diffuse pair selection, greedy Gromov-product packing, acylindricity fiber count and concentrated construction20–29 read. Definitions and full strongly-reduced/free/geodesic-extension proof11–13 retained. Standard hyperbolic four-point/discrete quasi-geodesic and acylindricity local-to-global results are explicitly cited existing research foundations. Does not claim finite-exponent Burnside quotient growth, whose additional aperiodic counting/small-cancellation core is not this unit. No symmetric-set assumption or uniform energy-free conclusion added. Incidental point-count labels in6.9 have the explicit packing bound and generous final10^6 constant; no separately claimed optimal numerical constant.
